newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's economy on track, but problems endure.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's economy on track, but problems endure.

text.p: Vietnam issued new economic data on Wednesday painting a picture of continued vigour but showing that problems with a yawning trade deficit were persisting.
The Government Statistics Office issued month-end estimates showing a trade gap of $420 million and a year-on-year industrial growth rate for January of 12.9 percent.
Earlier this week, the same department released data showing an inflation rate of 0.8 percent for January against 0.9 percent in the same month last year. The annual figure was put at 4.4 percent.

A report which accompanied Wednesday's figures said the January inflation was stable and therefore being seen as a sign that consumer spending around the Tet Lunar New Year festival -- which begins on February 6 -- would be restrained.
It said growth in the oil and gas sector had been a prime factor behind an industrial output level 12.9 percent higher than in the same month last year. Output of crude oil was up 20.2 percent.
But the figures continued to be slewed in favour of the foreign-invested sector which posted growth of 21.2 percent against 10.5 percent for Vietnam's state-owned sector.
News of the continued trade deficit was also less welcome.
The department said Vietnam was expected to have imported some $1 billion worth of goods by the end of this month, but exported only $580 million -- a deficit of $420 million.
Comparitive figures for the same month last year were not available, but Hanoi posted a deficit of $840 million for the first quarter of last year and a record shortfall for the year of $4.0 billion.
The issue has become a major policy concern for the government and prompted calls in some quarters to promote local products over imports and stirred debate over the merits of free trade.
